name: framework
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create a finished landscape 3:2 children's anatomy lesson illustration for Body School. Title "Your body's framework". White background, clean friendly anatomically sound shaded textbook illustration, navy headings, pale blue label bands, matching an elementary anatomy textbook. Three aligned full-body views of the same school-age child in the same relaxed standing pose: clothed child at left (T-shirt and shorts), simplified human skeleton in translucent body outline center, major skeletal muscles in translucent body outline right. Skeleton must have plausible skull, rib cage, spine, pelvis, paired limb bones, hands and feet; muscles simplified red, no gore. Headings "Your body", "Bones", "Skeletal muscles". Bottom three short labels "Support" "Protection" "Movement". Spacious, readable at 520px display width. Do not add tiny text or extraneous anatomy labels. No watermark.

name: bones-protect
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Finished 3:2 landscape elementary anatomy illustration for Body School. White background, navy readable sans serif headings, pale blue label boxes, warm ivory bones, gently shaded clean medical textbook illustration, friendly and non-gory. Title "Bones support and protect you". Three large side by side panels ONLY. Left: lateral cutaway skull enclosing orange brain, bone shell surrounding brain, label "Skull" with leader to bone, label "Brain" with leader to brain. Center: front rib cage with red heart between two pink lungs visibly behind ribs, label "Ribs" leader to rib, "Heart and lungs" leader to organs. Right: enlarged side cutaway segment of spine showing stacked vertebrae enclosing a yellow spinal cord within the vertebral canal, label "Spine" leader to vertebral bone and "Spinal cord" leader to yellow cord. The cord must pass inside the protective bony canal, behind vertebral bodies, not through solid bone bodies. Each panel has large bottom caption respectively "Protects the brain", "Protects the heart and lungs", "Protects the spinal cord". Anatomical relationships must be accurate, teaching simplified not photorealistic. Spacious clear large lettering, no tiny labels, no marrow inset, no watermark.

name: muscle-pairs
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create a precise elementary anatomy teaching diagram for Body School in 3:2 landscape, white background, navy headings, pale blue panel headers, soft ivory bones. Title "Muscles pull to make movement". Two side-by-side panels show the SAME right arm viewed from the side, shoulder upper left, elbow below shoulder. Left heading "Bending the elbow": upper arm vertical, forearm bent up and to the right, biceps on anterior (right-facing) upper arm visibly shorter and bulging red, triceps on posterior (left-facing) upper arm elongated pale salmon. Right heading "Straightening the elbow": upper arm in identical orientation, forearm almost straight down with slight forward angle, triceps on posterior left of upper arm short thick red, biceps anterior right long pale salmon. Forearm attaches anatomically at elbow; tendons connect each muscle across elbow to forearm bones. Show only upper-arm muscle pair, no extra muscles. Use simple curved arrows outside each elbow showing the relevant motion. Direct labels with leader lines in left panel "Contracts" to short biceps and "Relaxes" to long triceps; in right panel "Contracts" to short triceps and "Relaxes" to long biceps. Biceps and triceps locations must stay consistent between views. Bottom caption "Muscles pull. Pairs move bones in opposite directions." Readable large typography, no gore, no watermark.
